rows: A metal roof was blown off and trees blown down.
Recorded by cooperative observer on monthly report.
The National Weather Service in Fort Worth conducted a damage survey and found that a brief tornado formed northwest of Valley Mills and caused damage to trees along County Road 3310.

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth conducted a damage survey and concluded that a weak tornado touched down east-southeast of Clifton. Tree damage and minor roof and window damage was noted along CR 3350 and CR 3355.

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth conducted a damage survey and concluded a tornado formed east of Clifton. The tornado took a northeast track and went on to damage trees along CR 3355 just south of FM 708. The tornado also heavily damaged a turkey farm at the intersecti…

The National Weather Sevice in Fort Worth conducted a storm survey and concluded a tornado formed approximately two miles south of the Canyons subdivision on the west shore of Lake Whitney. Only tree damage was found, and the tornado dissipated after traveling less than a mile.
A tree was uprooted and a carport damaged.
Reported at State Highway 22 near Laguna Park.
Large trees were uprooted and several buildings damaged. Power lines were also downed.
Dozens of downed trees over northern Bosque county. Twenty-two structures sustained some type of wind damage, with four of those being mobile homes.
Trees were blown down and power was out in the Valley Mills area.
A large pecan tree was split at the intersection of Avenue H and Pecan Street.
Numerous outbuildings were damaged or destroyed as well as a mobile home. Trees were split and blown down.

An unoccupied trailer was flipped and several trees were blown down.
Large tree limbs fell onto power lines, causing power outages.
The roof of a porch was blown off.

A National Weather Service storm survey crew found evidence of damage consistent with EF-2 winds in Coryell County. Two homes were damaged to the point where most of their roof was removed. Several barns were destroyed as well, as were multiple pieces of farm and ranch equipment.…
